metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Electrochemistry — Half-Equations at Cathode and Anode (Electrolysis of HCl)
metadata.note: 4m: write ionic half-equations at cathode and anode during electrolysis of dilute hydrochloric acid. Cathode (reduction): 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂ (2m). Anode (oxidation): 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ (2m). Marks per half-equation: 1m correct species, 1m balanced electrons. Context: electrolysis of HCl(aq).

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q4b(iii) — Half-Equations at Cathode and Anode
question.text:
During electrolysis of dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl), ions are discharged at each electrode.

Write ionic half-equations for the reactions occurring at each electrode. (4 marks)

Cathode (negative electrode): (2 marks)

Anode (positive electrode): (2 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Electrolysis of dilute hydrochloric acid:

Ions present: H⁺(aq), Cl⁻(aq), OH⁻(aq) (from water), Na⁺ or other cations if present

Cathode (negative electrode — REDUCTION, OIL RIG: gain electrons):

2H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → H₂(g)

H⁺ ions are attracted to the negative electrode. They gain electrons and are reduced to hydrogen gas.

Anode (positive electrode — OXIDATION, OIL RIG: lose electrons):

2Cl⁻(aq) → Cl₂(g) + 2e⁻

Cl⁻ ions are attracted to the positive electrode. They lose electrons and are oxidised to chlorine gas.

Memory aid (OIL RIG): Oxidation Is Loss of electrons; Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

Note: In dilute acid, OH⁻ ions are also present but Cl⁻ is preferentially discharged at the anode in concentrated acid. In dilute HCl, both Cl₂ and O₂ may form at the anode, but the expected CSEC answer is Cl₂.

steps.label:
Cathode (−): positive ions (cations) attracted → gain electrons → REDUCTION
Anode (+): negative ions (anions) attracted → lose electrons → OXIDATION
Ions in HCl(aq): H⁺ and Cl⁻
Write the half-equation at the cathode. (2 marks)
Write the half-equation at the anode. (2 marks)

fields.label: Cathode: ion discharged and product formed = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: At the cathode, H⁺ ions from the acid are attracted, gain electrons, and are reduced to H₂ gas.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: At the cathode (negative electrode), positive ions (cations) are discharged. In HCl solution, H⁺ ions are attracted to the cathode, gain electrons (reduction), and form hydrogen gas H₂.

fields.label: Balanced cathode half-equation (with electrons): _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. Two hydrogen ions each gain one electron to form one H₂ molecule. Charge: left = 2(+1) + 2(−1) = 0; right = 0 ✓.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Cathode half-equation: 2H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → H₂(g). Check charge balance: left = 2(+) + 2(−) = 0; right = 0 ✓. Check atom balance: 2H left, 2H right ✓.

fields.label: Anode: ion discharged and product formed = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: At the anode, Cl⁻ ions are attracted, lose electrons, and are oxidised to Cl₂ gas.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: At the anode (positive electrode), negative ions (anions) are discharged. In HCl solution, Cl⁻ ions are attracted to the anode, lose electrons (oxidation), and form chlorine gas Cl₂.

fields.label: Balanced anode half-equation (with electrons): _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Two chloride ions each lose one electron to form one Cl₂ molecule. Charge: left = 2(−1) = −2; right = 2(−1) = −2 ✓.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Anode half-equation: 2Cl⁻(aq) → Cl₂(g) + 2e⁻. Check charge balance: left = 2(−1) = −2; right = 0 + 2(−1) = −2 ✓. Check atom balance: 2Cl left, 2Cl right ✓.
